title: Hot-tap a live pipe through its valve
instruction: Hot-tap the live pipe through the valve to cut out its coupon, return the tapping machine to its yellow stand, leave the valve shut with the blank on its outlet, and move both hands away.
context: Hot tapping cuts a branch into a pipe that stays in service: a tapping machine works through a valve, and the cut piece of pipe wall, the coupon, is held on the boring bar. It is done on refinery, gas and water lines where shutting down isn't practical.
setup: Positions are in cm from the arm bases' midpoint in x and the table's centre line in y, with +y toward the left arm. A blue-painted steel pipe, 6 cm square in section and 24 cm long, runs along x from x 16 to 40, centred at y -15.5 and 5 cm above the table, on two steel feet. From it an open-top channel runs along y on the axis x 28, 4 cm wide inside between walls 1 cm thick, its floor 2 cm above the table and its walls 7.5 cm tall: a steel stub from y -12.5 to -9.5, then a brass valve body from y -9.5 to -4.5. The valve's gate is a red aluminium plate 5.2 cm wide, 0.7 cm thick and 6 cm tall (90 g with its handle), lying across the channel with its centre at y -8, sliding along x and standing shut at the start; it opens 5 cm toward the arms. On its top a yellow handle post 2.4 cm across in x stands from y -9.6 to -8.35 up to 11.5 cm above the table. Two low steel ribs 0.4 cm thick and 1.5 cm tall lie across the valve's floor, from y -7.2 to -6.8 and from -4.9 to -4.5, and the outlet between them is uncovered. In the stub a sprung aluminium plug 3.6 cm wide stands for the pipe wall, its face at y -11.2 with an orange coupon disc 3.2 cm across on its top; pressing the face in takes up to 0.9 N over 6 mm. A dark steel saddle for the machine runs along y on the axis from the valve's end at y -4.5 to a rear stop at y 11.3: a pocket 6.6 cm wide inside, its floor 2 cm above the table and walls 1.5 cm above that. A tapping machine, 0.43 kg, stands on a yellow stand 12 x 24 cm, 2 mm thick, centred at (19, 20): a hollow aluminium housing 5 cm wide, 15 cm long along y and 4.5 cm tall, 3 mm walls, a hollow grip block 3 cm square and 4 cm tall on its top over its balance point, and a hollow aluminium boring bar 2 cm square, 21.3 cm long, its axis 3 cm above the housing's underside, sliding 5.6 cm through the housing toward -y with a yellow post 2.4 cm square on its tail. At the start the bar is fully retracted. An aluminium blank, 96 g, hangs by its flange across two steel rails 1 x 5 x 5.5 cm at (24, -25), with centres 4.8 cm apart in x: a flange 6 x 2.5 x 0.8 cm with a stem 3 x 0.8 x 5 cm under it and a knob 2.4 x 1.6 x 3 cm on top. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: Read at the end of the run; no early end. A hand is a gripper's fingertip midpoint; let go means both hands 6 cm or more from the part's box. The machine is seated with its underside within 6 mm of the saddle floor, its middle within 1.2 cm of (28, 3) cm along each axis, and flat within 5 degrees; on its stand within 4 cm of the stand's centre along each axis and 6 mm of its top, flat within 5 degrees. The gate is shut within 4 mm of its closed position. The blank is on the outlet with its flange's underside within 4 mm of the walls' top, within 6 mm of (28, -5.85) cm, and flat within 5 degrees. The coupon is cut once the machine is seated, the plug is pressed in 5 mm or more and the bar's nose is within 2 mm of its face, for 0.6 s; it stays cut for the rest of the trial and goes with the bar. 0 for good if the machine is off its saddle with the gate more than 5 mm open at any time after the cut, or if a part drops 1 cm below the table's top. Otherwise 0.1 for the machine seated and let go, without a cut; 0.3 for the coupon cut, the machine seated, or the machine off the saddle any other way; 0.6 for the coupon cut, the gate shut and the machine still seated and let go; 0.8 for the coupon cut, the gate shut and the machine on its stand and let go; 0.9 if the blank is also on the outlet and let go. 1.0 if both hands are also 6 cm or more from the middle of the gate's post and everything has been at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for the last 1 s. Otherwise 0. In a real trial, the coupon is a marked disc on a dummy plug and a marked disc on the bar's nose; a photo and tape measure the rest.
reset_notes: Put the machine back on the stand with the bar retracted, the gate shut, the blank on its rails and the coupon disc back on the plug. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation. Gate, plug spring and bar feed are real joints with real contact; gate and bar physically block each other. The cut is coded, gated on the bar pressing the sprung plug 5 mm with the machine seated. The coupon, its hole and the spray are visuals that switch; no material is removed and no fluid runs. Parts are square-section with a square pipe. A real trial uses a dummy bar and no pressure.
